overall_summary: Exoplanet chemistry and extreme cosmic environments are the primary growth drivers for FACTVERSE. Framing these space facts as first-person survival scenarios ('What If You Fell Into...') significantly boosts views and engagement compared to standard trivia. Conversely, brain facts, cognitive psychology, and generic space questions consistently underperform and struggle to capture audience retention.

winning_patterns.evidence: The Planet of Burning Ice (vWd0uYcEGh4) reached 1,055 views, TrES-2b (v1rrcZLdp4U) hit 1,025 views, and Supersonic Rubies (QXuqYERlqSo) achieved 721 views.
winning_patterns.action: Produce content focusing on exotic exoplanets with dramatic visual and chemical anomalies, emphasizing high-contrast concepts like burning ice or raining gems.

winning_patterns.pattern: 'What If You Fell Into...' Survival Scenarios
winning_patterns.evidence: What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice (8KEl0_pJ_68) reached 970 views and the $26 Nonillion Diamond Planet (6pwazIPnOHw) hit 494 views.
winning_patterns.action: Frame exoplanet facts as hypothetical first-person survival situations to increase viewer immersion and drive higher retention.

weak_patterns.evidence: Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories (r43-7nSn8SQ) generated only 10 views, and The Psychological Trick to Stop Songs (ef3ND4qiRHc) got 71 views.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standard cognitive psychology and brain trivia unless they can be framed with a highly dramatic, cinematic narrative.

weak_patterns.pattern: Generic Space Questions & Basic Astronomy Trivia
weak_patterns.evidence: Why Space Is Completely Silent (heB9rFCBRM8) generated only 33 views, and This Star Is Older Than the Universe (vFXHTmYITp4) got 11 views.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid basic space trivia that has been widely covered across YouTube; focus instead on highly specific, bizarre, and terrifying cosmic phenomena.

next_video.concept: What If You Fell Into the Planet That Rains Glass Sideways? (HD 189733b)
next_video.opening_direction: If you fell into this beautiful blue planet, you wouldn't drown in water—you'd be shredded by glass raining sideways at 5,400 miles per hour.
next_video.twist_direction: But the real nightmare isn't the wind. The atmosphere is packed with silicate particles, meaning you would literally breathe in molten glass before you even hit the surface.
next_video.reason: Combines the highly successful 'What If' survival framing with the top-performing exoplanet weather theme, matching the exact 21-second duration of the channel's highest-retention uploads.

experiment: Test a 21-second comparative survival Short ('Which Planet Kills You Faster?') comparing the burning ice planet against the sideways glass rain planet to see if a side-by-side comparison format increases average view duration.
